title: Sequential impact, friction and impulse timelines
prereq: P02 signed net impulse; P03 short-contact isolation; P06 contact energy; PH02 kinetic friction.
goals: Separate short impacts from a long sliding interval.
Apply friction impulse and work over their correct interval.
Check stopping distance before assuming a second collision can occur.

sections.heading: A timeline needs more than one ledger
sections.body: A sequence of contact, slide and a second contact has different physical assumptions in each stage. A brief contact may have negligible external impulse and permit conservation of the selected pair's momentum. During a long rough slide friction acts externally and changes the selected moving assembly's momentum.

sections.heading: Solve the first contact as a short event
sections.body: If the first moving cart latches onto a resting cart, use the two carts as the contact system and compute their immediately shared velocity from total signed momentum. Do not yet apply long-slide friction to the contact ledger.

sections.heading: Friction changes speed and can stop the second impact
sections.body: For a sliding assembly on a level track, F_f = −μMg while moving right and acceleration a = −μg. If the next obstacle is at distance d, compare its position with s_stop = v_start²/(2μg). If s_stop < d, the assembly stops before contact, and there is no second collision to analyse.

sections.heading: Only then solve the second contact
sections.body: If the sliding assembly reaches the next stationary body, find its velocity just BEFORE the second impact. Reapply short-contact momentum conservation for that new system. Separate contact energy conversion at each collision from the energy dissipated by friction during travel; do not double count.

sections.heading: Derive a reachability threshold before hypothesizing impact
sections.body: Conserve momentum separately during the short first collision; then treat the rough slide under frictional deceleration a=−μg. A proposed second collision exists only if the assembly reaches its obstacle while moving. For initial joined speed v₀ and obstacle distance L, stopping distance is s_stop=v₀²/(2μg). Equating s_stop=L gives the threshold μ_crit=v₀²/(2gL). For actual μ below this value, arrival speed is the positive root of v²=v₀²−2μgL. Only after the reach test supports an impact may the second sticking-momentum equation be applied; otherwise there is no second-contact speed.

worked.name: Foundation · friction-only stopping
worked.setup: A 2 kg cart at +4 m/s slides on level track with μ=0.2 and g=10 m/s².
steps: Initial K=16 J; friction work −4×4=−16 J.
worked.check: The long slide is NOT a momentum-conserving isolated interval.

worked.name: Connected · two contacts with friction between
worked.setup: A 1 kg cart at +8 m/s sticks to resting 3 kg cart, slides for 1 s at μ=0.1, then latches to resting 1 kg cart.
steps: Slide deceleration −1 m/s², just-before-second velocity +1 m/s.
worked.check: Do not carry +2 m/s directly into the second impact.

worked.name: Transfer · second impact never occurs
worked.setup: An assembly starts a 1 m rough section at +2 m/s with μ=0.4 and g=10 m/s².
steps: Obstacle is 1 m away, so no second contact occurs.
worked.check: Writing a second collision equation here would describe a physically impossible event.

trap.wrong: Conserve momentum across the entire rough slide or assume an obstacle is reached merely because it is present.
trap.repair: Split contact → friction → contact, calculate the pre-contact speed, and test stop distance before the second event.

assumptions: External friction is negligible DURING each very short impact but not during the slide.
μ is kinetic friction while moving; the model ceases to apply after stopping.
The second contact occurs only if the trajectory physically reaches the obstacle.

model.label: Teaching model: μ for a +3 m/s assembly with obstacle 1.5 m away

prompt.stem: On a right-positive track, a 1 kg cart at +6 m/s STICKS to a resting 2 kg cart in a brief first impact. The joined assembly travels on a rough horizontal strip toward a stationary 1 kg cart C, located 0.75 m ahead. Kinetic friction μ=0.20, g=10 m/s². Friction during brief impact is negligible and C will stick IF REACHED. The second collision is NOT guaranteed. Find first joined speed, threshold μ_crit for reaching C, whether C is hit, speed immediately before C and the final speed if it sticks.
prompt.prediction: Which reachability test must precede a second-impact momentum calculation?

fields.label: Limiting μ for just reaching C
Speed just before C if reached
Joined speed after C if reached

prompt.boundaryPrompt: Change ONLY friction to μ=0.30 while preserving first-joined speed and the 0.75 m distance to C. Does a second collision occur? Give the assembly's stopping distance.

researchNote: Unlike the Connected anchor with guaranteed impact, the protected question makes the coefficient threshold and existence of event three the decisive work.
